name: BlackRock Daily Reinvestment Stablecoin Reserve Vehicle
oneLiner: BRSRV is BlackRock's registered Treasury, repo and cash fund share, targeting $1 NAV with income reinvestment and Securitize redemption.
collateral: Cash, U.S. Treasury obligations with no more than 93 days to maturity and Treasury-secured overnight repurchase agreements in BlackRock Daily Reinvestment Stablecoin Reserve Vehicle. October 14, 2026 listed securities comprise approximately 61.8874% Treasury bills and 38.1126% overnight repo by market value; BNY Mellon is custodian and accounting-services provider, Securitize is transfer agent. These weights cover disclosed securities, not total fund net assets or a whole-token liability reconciliation.
pegMechanism: Registered government money-market OnChain share targeting $1 NAV. Income is declared daily and, unless the shareholder elects cash dividends, reinvested in additional shares on the next business day. New subscription and reinvestment tokens have a 24-hour peer-transfer lock, but remain available for redemption and relocation between the same investor's whitelisted wallets. Securitize administers whitelisted subscriptions, transfers and redemptions across Ethereum, Tempo and Solana. Access is generally limited to U.S. investors with a $3 million initial minimum, which may be waived. Good-order redemption requests received before 5 p.m. Eastern on eligible business days ordinarily settle by same-day federal-funds wire when the custodian is open; the fund reserves up to seven days, with specified legal/emergency suspension exceptions. The prospectus charges no redemption fee, but shareholder-initiated transactions generally incur variable network gas and intermediary charges may apply. Redemption processing remains available off-chain during blockchain outages. Peer transfers do not constitute a public trading market. Sponsor support and principal preservation are not guaranteed.

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: The exact deployment represents a USD short-duration money-market fund share with ordinary NAV redemption. The tbill family models the fund/NAV mechanism; it does not imply Treasury-only holdings. This is a distinct registered fund, not BUIDL.
